chunks: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya narrated from Abu Ja'far al-Nahwi, from Abu al-Jawza', from al-Husayn ibn 'Alwan, from 'Amr ibn Khallad, from 'Asim ibn Abi al-Najud al-Asadi, from Ibn 'Umar, from al-Hasan ibn 'Ali (peace be upon him), who said:

I heard my father, 'Ali ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon him), saying that the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Any Muslim man who sits in his place of prayer where he prayed Fajr, remembering Allah until the sun rises, will have the reward of the Hajj of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family), and his sins will be forgiven. If he sits there until the time for prayer is established, and prays two or four rak'ahs, his past sins will be forgiven, and he will have the reward of the Hajj of the House of Allah.'

key_terms.كَحَاجِّ رَسُولِ اللَّهِ: like the reward of the Messenger of Allah's Hajj

ai.seo_question: What is the reward for sitting in prayer after Fajr until sunrise?
ai.summary: Recorded in Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* via a chain linking back to Imam al-Hasan (AS), this hadith emphasizes the virtue of *al-Zuhr* (the mid-morning prayer) performed after the sun's rise. It highlights the continuity of worship by connecting the post-Fajr dhikr session directly to the reward of the Prophet’s Hajj, while the subsequent voluntary prayer ensures the forgiveness of past sins, reinforcing the Shia emphasis on consistent, structured devotional practices.
